answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 268 answers need 268 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the pigment index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the tide audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the hollow identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator burns for 268 runs and collects one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
